annotatedCaseStudies.title: Corpus A Empirical False-Familiarity Case 1: B02 (CRITICALITY_DIVERGENCE)
annotatedCaseStudies.strategicContext: Corpus A empirical game pair from B02 (https://www.chess.com/game/live/100122267045 ply 19, Arysya vs Hikaru) and (https://www.chess.com/game/live/101686916789 ply 19, Snowflake vs Hikaru). Both share static similarity 0.948 with identical turn (w) and material balance.
annotatedCaseStudies.failureMechanism: Despite high static structural match (sim=0.948), dynamic evaluations diverge by 134 cp (u: 47 cp, best: e3g5 vs v: 181 cp, best: d4d5). Criticality gap diff is 159 cp.

annotatedCaseStudies.title: Sicilian Dragon Yugoslav Attack: Castling King Safety Divergence
annotatedCaseStudies.strategicContext: Standard Yugoslav pawn structure and piece configuration, both Black to move. White is uncastled in U vs castled queenside in V.
annotatedCaseStudies.failureMechanism: Castling state divergence transforms tactical feasibility: in V, Black executes immediate central break ...d6-d5 with tempo against queenside king.

annotatedCaseStudies.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Active Outpost vs Immobile Target
annotatedCaseStudies.strategicContext: Both Black to move with identical minor piece deployment. U retains bishop on c5, V has c-pawns traded with d5 fixed.
annotatedCaseStudies.failureMechanism: Pawn structure fixity deprives Black of the c4 outpost, turning passive pieces into immobile targets.

annotatedCaseStudies.title: King's Indian Defense: Closed Center Castling Timing Divergence
annotatedCaseStudies.strategicContext: Locked center (d5 vs d6/e5) characteristic of KID classical mainlines, both White to move. White uncastled in U vs castled in V.
annotatedCaseStudies.failureMechanism: White king position alters defensive resource availability against Black thematic ...f7-f5 kingside thrust.

annotatedCaseStudies.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Castling King Safety Divergence
annotatedCaseStudies.strategicContext: Caro-Kann Advance pawn triangle (c6-d5-e6 vs c2-d4-e5), both Black to move. Full 16-piece armies on both sides. White uncastled in U vs castled in V.
annotatedCaseStudies.failureMechanism: Castling safety divergence: in U White king remains on e1 exposing central pins, whereas in V White has castled, allowing tactical sacrifices on e6.
